It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the "unsearchable riches" of Christ while witnessing a world where children are often treated as "administrative anomalies" rather than "vessels for honor," and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the status of those born outside of traditional covenant structures and the mothers who raise them alone in this hour? [13, 23, 119, 361, 1503, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling "overwhelmed and desperate" by the "noise and tumult" of a society that offers "moral judgment" as a "spiritual placebo" for its own lack of compassion, or are you seeking a "settled certainty" to anchor your soul in the truth that "God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation"—including the life of every child? [13, 15, 20, 68, 146, 1143, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many "shave off the edges" of the truth to protect "religious leaders" who "strain out a gnat and swallow a camel," we must return to the "external Word" to see how the Lord personally governs the "vicissitudes of life" by demanding that we "seek justice" and "defend the fatherless" (Isaiah 1:17; Matthew 23:24) [8, 11, 28, 160, 1091, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that "nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan," and therefore, the care of the vulnerable is not a secondary "humanitarianism" but a "binding and authoritative mandate" from the King of Kings [5, 11, 21, 32, 71, 101, 1312, 1333, 1503, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Outcast and the God Who Sees**

**Verse**
“Then she called the name of the LORD who spoke to her, You-Are-the-God-Who-Sees; for she said, ‘Have I also here seen Him who sees me?’ ” (Genesis 16:13). [247, 938, 979, Conversation History]. “ ‘Arise, lift up the lad and hold him with your hand, for I will make him a great nation’ ” (Genesis 21:18). [393, 914, 989, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The "record of history" reveals that God did not abandon Hagar when she was "cast out" as a "bondwoman," for He is a "loving, beneficent Father" who "hears the cry of affliction" [6, 8, 249, 914, 938, 942, Conversation History]. Even though Ishmael was born through "sinfully yielding" to a custom of the day rather than waiting on the promise, God "visited" the mother in the wilderness and "remembered" the child’s future [246, 250, 937, 942, 1068, Conversation History]. For the Reformed believer, this proves that "unbelief is the seed" of human cruelty, but "every good gift and every perfect gift is from above," and God "takes the things that happen in our lives and puts them together for good" (James 1:17; Romans 8:28) [1, 23, 62, 1143, 1201, 1339, 1381, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should "not be deceived" by those who think a child’s value is determined by their "genealogical connection," for "God shows no partiality" and the "Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands" (Acts 10:34; Acts 7:48) [5, 11, 13, 59, 79, 142, 612, 1042, 1316, 1502, 1646, Conversation History]. Recognize that "the Lord knows your hearts," and He is "not pleased" with a "religious track record" that ignores the "broken heart" of a mother alone (Luke 16:15; Lamentations 1:20) [4, 11, 152, 830, 1090, 1111, 1430, 1551, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: From Stigma to Standing**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the "religious leaders" relied on "lineage and circumcision" to define the "holy seed," and those of "illegitimate birth" were historically "excluded from the congregation" (Deuteronomy 23:2) [207, 718, 1214, 1352, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our "inheritance," revealing that "in Christ Jesus... there is neither slave nor free," for we are all "redeemed from the curse of the law" and "brought near by the blood of Christ" (Galatians 3:28; Ephesians 2:13) [13, 26, 32, 136, 142, 167, 399, 440, 733, 1023, 1313, 1426, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Mandatory Shield for the Vulnerable**

**Verse**
“ ‘He administers justice for the fatherless and the widow, and loves the stranger, giving him food and clothing’ ” (Deuteronomy 10:18). [329, Conversation History]. “ ‘You shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child. If you afflict them in any way, and they cry at all to Me, I will surely hear their cry; and My wrath will become hot’ ” (Exodus 22:22–24). [83, 269, 1056, 1086, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Reformed theology—upheld by **John MacArthur**—asserts that God "reserved His special attention" for those who "often had no one to care for them" [270, 1086, Conversation History]. The law was not merely a list of "ritualized ceremonies," but a demand for "pure and undefiled religion" which includes "defending their families against criminal... aggression" and "taking no business advantage" of the destitute [158, 271, 449, 742, 825, 894, 1087, 1351, Conversation History]. God "abominates anyone who would justify an evildoer" who exploits a single mother, for "the Lord will respond to the prayer of the destitute" and "He heals the brokenhearted" (Proverbs 17:15; Psalm 102:17; 147:3) [11, 23, 88, 144, 479, 1033, 1143, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
"Trade in your worry for trust," knowing that the Lord is a "defender of widows" and "a father of the fatherless" (Psalm 68:5) [6, 94, 201, 469, 1408, 1515, Conversation History]. You must "discipline your mind" to recognize that "every tree is known by its own fruit," and a church that does not "pull them out of the fire" of poverty and neglect is like a "whitewashed tomb" (Luke 6:44; Jude 23; Matthew 23:27) [6, 13, 116, 122, 146, 188, 1349, 1406, 1486, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of Vengeance**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, God warned that His "wrath" would reduce the families of abusers to the "same status" of being "without spouse or parents" through "military invasions" (Exodus 22:24) [270, 1056, 1087, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our "warfare," teaching that "the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh," but we still "contend earnestly" by "ascribing greatness to our God" through the "righteous deeds of the saints" (2 Corinthians 10:4; Jude 3; Revelation 19:8) [11, 21, 32, 43, 92, 125, 1081, 1210, 1313, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: Adoption into the Covenant Family**

**Verse**
“But when the fullness of the time had come, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman, born under the law, to redeem those who were under the law, that we might receive the adoption as sons” (Galatians 4:4–5). [35, 139, 411, 731, 1256, Conversation History]. “For you have not received a spirit of slavery leading to fear again, but you have received a spirit of adoption as sons by which we cry out, ‘Abba! Father!’ ” (Romans 8:15). [140, 141, 153, 189, 190, 416, 732, 1102, 1104, 1286, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Paul Washer**—teaches that we were all "spiritual orphans" under the "cruel oppression of sin," yet God "intervened to rescue us" [11, 102, 144, 145, 131, 1331, 1503, Conversation History]. This "miracle of adoption" means that the believer’s standing is not based on "human effort" or "bloodlines," but on the "finished work" of Christ [11, 24, 126, 129, 144, 145, 415, 1313, 1445, 1503, Conversation History]. Just as King David adopted Mephibosheth—the "crippled son" of his enemy's house—and "invited him to dine regularly at his own royal table," so God "exchanges our filthy rags for robes of righteousness" [134, 147, 148, 166, 1315, 1491, 1617, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
"Your life is not your own" because you were "bought at a price," and your "sole objective" is to find "rest" in the Father’s "lavish endowment" (1 Corinthians 6:20; James 1:17) [12, 18, 101, 113, 212, 1132, 1138, 1262, 1339, 1406, 1670, Conversation History]. You should "wait for His Son from heaven," knowing that "the Lord knows those who are His" and "He will never allow the righteous to be shaken" (1 Thessalonians 1:10; 2 Timothy 2:19; Psalm 55:22) [11, 24, 25, 41, 45, 87, 147, 176, 201, 211, 222, 285, 300, 313, 332, 361, 405, 414, 444, 591, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual to Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, "man-made representations" and "legal minutiae" were often used to "establish their own righteousness" while being "ignorant of God’s righteousness" (Romans 10:3) [8, 176, 177, 316, 1091, 1448, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our view, revealing that "the true circumcision" is "that of the heart," and our "victory" is found in the "Spirit of adoption" that grants "childlike assurance" rather than "legalistic fear" (Romans 2:29; Romans 8:15) [13, 140, 141, 231, 233, 239, 295, 359, 802, 842, 1104, 1214, 1286, 1313, 1426, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Church’s Obligation Beyond Moral Judgment**

**Verse**
“Pure and undefiled religion before God and the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their trouble, and to keep oneself unspotted from the world” (James 1:27). [449, 742, 825, Conversation History]. “ ‘In that day you shall be ashamed of all your deeds in which you transgress against Me; for then I will take away from your midst those who rejoice in your pride, and you shall no longer be haughty in My holy mountain’ ” (Zephaniah 3:11). [1056, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Voddie Baucham**—asserts that "Jesus’ definition of leadership is one of self-sacrificing service," and the church is to be a "holy place where sin is despised" but where the vulnerable find "provision [and] protection" [102, 134, 1406, 1421, Conversation History]. Our "common salvation" compels us to "bear one another’s burdens" and "rescue those who have been led astray" by "savage wolves" (Galatians 6:2; Jude 23) [17, 31, 391, 449, 458, 664, 760, 825, 1152, 1246, 1270, 1349, 1358, 1389, 1425, 1440, 1461, 1515, Conversation History]. While we must "not be conformed to this world," we "refuse to yield submission" to any "spirit of fraud" that uses "religion" as a "cloak for vice" or neglect (Romans 12:2; 1 Peter 2:16) [11, 12, 19, 91, 146, 212, 1144, 1316, 1502, 1503, 1532, 1638, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
"Never become so involved in this world" that you treat the "more sure word" as a "platform for your own ego," for your "chief mission" is to "testify to the gospel of the grace of God" (Acts 20:24) [21, 27, 28, 51, 130, 323, 782, 843, 861, 975, 1022, 1503, 1623, Conversation History]. You must "discipline your body and bring it into subjection," finding "joy, satisfaction, [and] contentment" in "ascribing greatness to our God" through mercy (1 Corinthians 9:27; Deuteronomy 32:3) [11, 13, 20, 36, 79, 110, 116, 1311, 1406, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, the "priests" were "messengers of the LORD" who were to "keep knowledge" and "decide on all appeals" to ensure "justice for all" (Malachi 2:7; Exodus 18:26) [847, 848, 1092, 1317, 1365, 1473, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our "witness," showing that "we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image," which is an image of "tender mercies, kindness, humility, meekness, [and] longsuffering" (2 Corinthians 3:18; Colossians 3:12) [382, 541, 569, 602, 618, 619, 675, 868, 870, 1218, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 201, 211, 222, 285, 300, 313, 324, 332, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: It Encourages Hope In the midst of a hostile world that’s falling apart, God is our Father, and He’ll take care of our future. If an earthly father will spare no effort to help and protect his children, how much more will our Heavenly Father love, protect, and help us (Matt. 7:11)? It Removes Loneliness Even if we are rejected and abandoned by family, friends, or even fellow believers, we know that our Heavenly Father will never leave us (Heb. 13:5). To drive away loneliness, God’s presence is all a believer ever needs.

I was recently shown an essay posted on the Internet by an anonymous author (presumably a pastor), who reimagined the parable of the prodigal son from a feminist perspective and thereby intentionally turned the entire story on its head. In this person’s freehanded reinterpretation, we’re encouraged to visualize the father as an aloof family patriarch who thoughtlessly drives his younger son away by neglect. This one new facet of the story “changes everything,” the unknown writer solemnly (and shamelessly) informs us. The son’s demand for the early inheritance now “alludes to a prior and perhaps long-standing family strain, [and] the boy’s dissolute living may be his effort to ‘buy’ … affiliation and belonging,” which he had long craved but did not have because the father had so carelessly marginalized him. Rather than a self-indulgent “plot to sow his wild oats,” the prodigal’s pursuit of a reckless lifestyle thus becomes a desperate cry for help.2

Esther is another notable Old Testament example of adoption. When her parents died, she was taken in by Mordecai, her older cousin. He cared for her as a father, making sure to look after her welfare (cf. Esth. 2:5–11). Even after she became queen, Esther continued to look to Mordecai for parental guidance and encouragement. One of the most heart-warming accounts in the Old Testament is that of Mephibosheth, who for all practical purposes was adopted by King David.4 Mephibosheth was the crippled son of Jonathan, David’s closest friend, and sole surviving descendant of King Saul. After learning about Mephibosheth, David invited him to dine regularly at his own royal table. He also gave him the land that had previously belonged to his grandfather Saul (2 Sam. 9:1– 13).
